newsitem.title: USA: Maine Public Service says might default on bonds.
newsitem.headline: Maine Public Service says might default on bonds.

text.p: Maine Public Service Co has warned investors that it might default on about $15 million of tax-exempt, revenue bonds because of the problems caused by the closing of the troubled Maine Yankee nuclear plant.
"Yes, we think it's possible that we may (default) for the first quarter of 1997," said the company's controller.

Kurt Tornquist explained that the company, which is holding discussions with banks, issued the warning in an 8-K form filed on January 31 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Bank of New York Co Inc provided a letter of credit that was used to back the bonds.

In the same filing with the SEC, the utility said that because of the Maine Yankee plant it also faced a potential default on a revolving credit line of up to $10 million, of which only about $900,000 is outstanding.
The utility feared coverage tests of the bonds and the line of credit might be violated, Tornquist said.

Maine Yankee has had safety-related shutdowns and is under close scrutiny by federal regulators. The plant and Entergy Corp recently signed an interim contract that calls for Entergy to run Maine Yankee while a longer-term, management pact is negotiated.
Maine Public Service said it had just over $41 million of long-term debt outstanding at year-end.
